questions.question: What does iron do in the body?
questions.answer: Iron is an essential nutrient. It is required for hemoglobin, myoglobin, heme enzymes, and mitochondrial enzymes, according to [[sources/ufelle2021-metals-chapter|Ufelle & Barchowsky 2021]].

questions.question: Can iron be toxic even though it's an essential nutrient?
questions.answer: Yes. [[sources/ufelle2021-metals-chapter|Ufelle & Barchowsky 2021]] attaches iron to the wiki as both an essential nutrient and a toxicity concern. The two toxicity pathways it identifies are acute iron poisoning and chronic iron overload.

questions.question: What are the main ways iron causes harm?
questions.answer: The page identifies two mechanisms of iron toxicity: acute poisoning and chronic iron overload, as described in [[sources/ufelle2021-metals-chapter|Ufelle & Barchowsky 2021]]. The page does not yet detail dose levels, affected populations, or specific health outcomes for either pathway.

questions.question: Does this page cover iron levels in specific foods or products?
questions.answer: Not yet. This is a source-map stub created during the re-ingest of [[sources/ufelle2021-metals-chapter|Ufelle & Barchowsky 2021]], and substantive iron-specific expansion awaits a dedicated iron ingest. Only one source is currently attached to the page.
